# Hello World!

A simple Git repository demonstrating basic Git commands.

## Setup Instructions

### 1. Create Project Directory

Creates a directory for your project:

```bash
mkdir ~/Hello-World
```

### 2. Navigate to Directory

Changes to your newly created directory:

```bash
cd ~/Hello-World
```

### 3. Initialize Git Repository

Sets up the necessary Git files:

```bash
git init
```

Expected output:
```
Initialized empty Git repository in /Users/your_user_directory/Hello-World/.git/
```

### 4. Create README File

```bash
touch README
```

refactorings.summary: The README requires significant refactoring to meet modern documentation standards. Six refactoring opportunities identified: 3 high-impact (formatting, separation, structure), 2 medium-impact (path placeholder, command presentation), and 1 low-impact (newline at EOF). While this is a documentation file rather than code, applying these refactoring principles will dramatically improve usability, readability, and maintainability.

recommendations.description: Apply proper markdown formatting to README. Add code blocks, clear section headings, and separate commands from descriptions. This is the most critical improvement needed.
Rename README to README.md to enable proper markdown rendering on GitHub and follow modern repository conventions.
Add proper document structure with title, overview, prerequisites, setup instructions, and next steps sections. Include a table of contents for better navigation.
Replace macOS-specific path examples with platform-agnostic placeholders or provide examples for all major operating systems (macOS, Linux, Windows).
